skill.name: lamindb
skill.description: Guides LaminDB workflows for biological data management, lineage tracking, ontology curation, integrations, and deployment planning.
skill.summary: Use LaminDB to organize, validate, query, and trace biological research data.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown code spans, LaminDB import aliases, placeholder URLs, and biological validation examples. Confirmed risks are legitimate operational guidance that handles credentials, sudo commands, hidden API-key storage, temporary exports, and destructive cache deletion.

remediation.issue: Credential examples use shell environment variables and default MinIO values.
remediation.suggestion: Replace default values with clearly invalid placeholders and add guidance for approved secrets management.

remediation.issue: Deployment examples include sudo commands and system environment file edits.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and provide non-root alternatives where possible.
Use a user-controlled private directory and document permission requirements for sensitive research data.

remediation.issue: Cache cleanup examples use shutil.rmtree on the LaminDB cache directory.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users that the operation is destructive and suggest safer cache management commands first.
Prefer HTTPS endpoints and state that HTTP should be limited to trusted local development.

content.value_statement: Biology teams need traceable data that stays queryable across files, workflows, and annotations. This skill guides LaminDB setup, curation, lineage tracking, and integration patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains LaminDB artifacts, records, runs, transforms, features, and collections.
Shows query patterns for artifacts, metadata, features, and large datasets.
Guides schema validation and curation for DataFrames, AnnData, MuData, and SpatialData.
Describes Bionty ontology import, validation, standardization, and annotation workflows.
Documents integrations with Nextflow, Snakemake, W&B, MLflow, Git, and cloud storage.
Covers local, cloud, PostgreSQL, and shared deployment patterns.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a managed LaminDB service.
It assumes users understand Python, biological data formats, and their storage policies.
It does not validate real credentials, cloud permissions, or production security controls.
Some examples require adaptation for current LaminDB versions and local infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Curate single-cell datasets
use_cases.description: Validate AnnData metadata, standardize cell types, and save traceable artifacts for later querying.

use_cases.title: Build governed data catalogs
use_cases.description: Define features, schemas, and ontology terms so research datasets remain searchable and reproducible.

use_cases.title: Plan production deployments
use_cases.description: Compare local, cloud, PostgreSQL, storage, cache, and workflow integration patterns for team use.

prompt_templates.title: Start a LaminDB project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a LaminDB project for my biology dataset. Include storage, schema, and first artifact steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design validation schemas
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LaminDB validation approach for my AnnData metadata. Include required fields and ontology checks.

prompt_templates.title: Query research data
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to query LaminDB artifacts by tissue, condition, creator, date, and feature annotations.

prompt_templates.title: Architect team deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review a LaminDB deployment for a team using cloud storage, PostgreSQL, Git sync, and workflow managers.

output_examples.input: Plan a LaminDB setup for single-cell data with ontology validation.
output_examples.output: A staged plan covering instance setup, schema design, Bionty imports, curation checks, and artifact registration.

output_examples.input: Explain how to find all treated PBMC datasets without loading every file.
output_examples.output: A query-first workflow using artifact filters, feature metadata, tabular previews, and selective loading.

output_examples.input: Compare local SQLite and cloud PostgreSQL deployments for a small biology team.
output_examples.output: A tradeoff summary covering collaboration, storage durability, performance, credentials, backups, and migration steps.

best_practices: Define schemas and ontology mappings before registering large curated datasets.
Track analyses with lineage metadata before saving derived artifacts.
Use explicit user-approved credential and storage settings for cloud deployments.
anti_patterns: Do not load large artifacts before narrowing results with metadata queries.
Do not store real cloud secrets in shared examples, notebooks, or logs.
Do not clear caches or change system directories without explicit confirmation.

faq.question: What is LaminDB used for?
faq.answer: LaminDB organizes biological datasets with queryable metadata, lineage, validation, and ontology-based annotations.

faq.question: Does this skill install LaminDB?
faq.answer: No. It explains setup commands and workflow patterns that users can review before running.

faq.question: Can it help with single-cell data?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes AnnData, MuData, SpatialData, ontology validation, and artifact tracking patterns.

faq.question: Does it support cloud storage planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers S3, GCS, S3-compatible storage, PostgreSQL, cache settings, and deployment tradeoffs.

faq.question: How should credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Use user-approved secrets management and avoid pasting real keys into prompts, examples, logs, or shared files.

faq.question: Can it replace a data governance review?
faq.answer: No. It provides technical guidance, but regulated biological data still needs local compliance review.
